what: The Verify Seal battery (instruments/seal/battery.py): the commitment SHA256('verify-seal-v1\n' || salt || SHA256(archive)) opened under planted forgeries, and since 2026-11-05 the v2 per-file salted manifest (one file revealed under a sealed manifest, the whole bundle opened) under its own forgeries and two red controls — each must come back REFUTED or REFUSED, never CERTIFIED — plus the determinism check (the same contents written another way re-derive the sealed digest), the date rule (an anchor dated after the claimed date refuses), the unconfirmed-anchor cases, and the one-line shell re-derivation against the Python digest; three red controls on a deliberately broken opener. Run in a temporary directory with a temporary git registry; no network, no ots client.

forgeries.forgery: one byte flipped in the archive
forgeries.reason: the digest does not re-derive; what differs is the archive: its sha256 is not the one sealed (a byte, a file or a name inside it differs)

forgeries.forgery: wrong salt (64 hex, another value)
forgeries.reason: the digest does not re-derive; what differs is the salt: salt.hex is not the salt drawn at sealing

forgeries.forgery: truncated salt (60 hex)
forgeries.reason: salt.hex is not exactly 64 lowercase hex characters (60 character(s))

forgeries.forgery: salt with a trailing newline
forgeries.reason: salt.hex is not exactly 64 lowercase hex characters (65 character(s), ends in a newline)

forgeries.forgery: salt missing
forgeries.reason: salt.hex is missing: without the salt the digest cannot be re-derived (a lost salt is an unopenable seal)

forgeries.forgery: archive missing
forgeries.reason: archive.tar is missing: without the bytes there is nothing to re-derive (the researcher holds it)

forgeries.forgery: a file added inside the folder (re-archived under the sealed salt)
forgeries.reason: the digest does not re-derive; what differs is the archive: its sha256 is not the one sealed (a byte, a file or a name inside it differs)

forgeries.reason: the digest does not re-derive; what differs is the archive: its sha256 is not the one sealed (a byte, a file or a name inside it differs)

forgeries.forgery: seal.json's digest edited
forgeries.reason: the digest does not re-derive; what differs is the recorded digest itself: archive and salt are the sealed ones, so seal.json's digest was edited

forgeries.forgery: seal.json's version edited
forgeries.reason: seal.json version 'verify-seal-v0' is not verify-seal-v1 or verify-seal-v2; this opener reads only those

forgeries.forgery: seal.json missing
forgeries.reason: seal.json is missing; the bundle cannot be opened without the recorded digest

forgeries.forgery: v2: the revealed file's bytes differ by one bit
forgeries.reason: the revealed bytes do not re-derive the manifest's sha256 at index 3 (the name does): the bytes differ from the sealed ones

forgeries.forgery: v2: the right bytes revealed under another name
forgeries.reason: the revealed name does not re-derive the manifest's path_hash at index 3 (the bytes do): the file was sealed under another name

forgeries.forgery: v2: the revealed file claimed at another index of the manifest
forgeries.reason: neither the revealed bytes nor the revealed name re-derive the manifest's entry 0 under this salt: not the file that was sealed there

forgeries.forgery: v2: a revealed file absent from the manifest (index beyond it)
forgeries.reason: reveal.json names index 99, but the sealed manifest holds 4 file(s): no such sealed file

forgeries.forgery: v2: another salt for the revealed file
forgeries.reason: neither the revealed bytes nor the revealed name re-derive the manifest's entry 3 under this salt: not the file that was sealed there

forgeries.forgery: v2: the manifest edited (a sha256 changed, canonical form kept): its seal no longer re-derives
forgeries.reason: the manifest's digest does not re-derive; what differs is the manifest: its sha256 is not the one sealed — nothing under it is decided

forgeries.forgery: v2: the manifest re-serialised with spaces (not canonical)
forgeries.reason: manifest.json is not in canonical form (sorted keys, no spaces, one trailing newline): re-derive it with manifest_bytes

forgeries.forgery: v2: the manifest missing from the package
forgeries.reason: manifest.json is missing

forgeries.forgery: v2: another manifest salt
forgeries.reason: the manifest's digest does not re-derive; what differs is the salt: salt.hex is not the manifest's salt — nothing under it is decided

forgeries.forgery: v2: the package's seal.json claims v1
forgeries.reason: seal.json version 'verify-seal-v1' is not verify-seal-v2; this verifier reads only verify-seal-v2

forgeries.forgery: v2: one byte flipped in the whole bundle's archive (the manifest intact)
forgeries.reason: the manifest's seal re-derives but 1 file(s) do not: index 2 (notes/plan.txt): the bytes or the name do not re-derive the manifest's entry

forgeries.forgery: v2: one per-file salt replaced in salts.json
forgeries.reason: the manifest's seal re-derives but 1 file(s) do not: index 0 (données.txt): the bytes or the name do not re-derive the manifest's entry

cases.reason: the archive and salt re-derive the recorded digest; 1 anchor(s) confirmed; the bytes were held by 2026-11-03 (on or before the claimed 2026-11-03)

cases.case: claimed --by a date AFTER the anchor (a later claim is weaker, still decidable)
cases.reason: the archive and salt re-derive the recorded digest; 1 anchor(s) confirmed; the bytes were held by 2026-11-03 (on or before the claimed 2026-12-01)

cases.case: an anchor dated after the claimed date (--by 2026-11-01, anchor 2026-11-03)
cases.reason: the digest re-derives and the earliest confirmed anchor is dated 2026-11-03, after the claimed 2026-11-01: possession by 2026-11-01 is not decidable from the anchors (an earlier anchor would decide it)

cases.case: no anchor at all
cases.reason: the digest re-derives, but no public anchor is in the bundle: the date is only a local claim. Decidable once `stamp` anchors it (digest.txt.ots and/or a registry commit in anchors.json)

red_controls.red: an opener that certifies a mismatched digest IS caught (a flipped byte comes back CERTIFIED under it)
an opener that ignores the claimed date IS caught (a date before the anchor comes back CERTIFIED under it)
an opener that tolerates a newline after the salt IS caught (bytes.fromhex strips it; the strict rule is what refuses)
v2: a verifier that skips the salted path check IS caught (the right bytes under another name come back CERTIFIED under it)
v2: a verifier that skips the salted file hash IS caught (flipped bytes come back CERTIFIED under it)
